answer.rationale: p99 latency spike on write path with heavy settlement traffic at peak. Rollback is blocked by compliance-mandated security patch. Circuit breaker and failover address availability but not the underlying latency pressure. Capacity addition is safe but slower. Routing read queries to replicas (memory_b5) proved effective at reducing primary load and recovering latency the same day without touching writes or requiring rollback. This preserves the security patch compliance requirement, alleviates primary pressure immediately, and maintains write durability during settlement peak. Verifying b5 confirms the mechanism worked at similar load conditions.
